questions.question:
In which of following reaction on increasing pressure products do not increase :–
"
questions.explanation:
A. Question:
In which of the following reactions does increasing pressure not increase the yield of products?
B. Given Data:

\tReaction 1: 2SO2(g) + O2(g) ⇌ 2SO3(g)
\tReaction 2: NH4HS(s) ⇌ NH3(g) + H2S(g)
\tReaction 3: N2O4(g) ⇌ 2NO2(g)

C. Concept:


\tLe Chatelier's Principle: When a system at equilibrium is subjected to stress, the system will shift in a direction that tends to counteract the stress and re-establish equilibrium.
\tEffect of Pressure:
\t
\t\tIncreasing pressure favors the side of the reaction with fewer moles of gas.
\t
\t

D. Mathematical Calculation:
1. Analyze each reaction:


\tReaction 1: 3 moles of gas on the left, 2 moles of gas on the right. Increasing pressure will shift the equilibrium to the right (towards products).
\tReaction 2: 0 moles of gas on the left, 2 moles of gas on the right. Increasing pressure will shift the equilibrium to the left (towards reactants).
\tReaction 3: 1 mole of gas on the left, 2 moles of gas on the right. Increasing pressure will shift the equilibrium to the left (towards reactants).

E. Final Answer:
2. NH4HS(s) ⇌ NH3(g) + H2S(g) and
3. N2O4(g) ⇌ 2NO2(g)
In both reactions 2 and 3, increasing pressure will not increase the yield of products.

questions.question: What are the disc-shaped structures present on the sides of the centromere in chromosomes called?
questions.explanation:
Solution : 
The kinetochore is a disc-shaped structure that forms on the sides of the centromere of a chromosome. It serves as the attachment point for spindle fibers during cell division (mitosis and meiosis). The kinetochore is essential for proper chromosome alignment and separation during cell division.

Final Answer :
Option (3)

questions.question: The number of chromosomes becomes double in :
If a diploid cell has 10 Pg DNA in G1-stage of interphase, what will be the amount of DNA in each daughter cell after meiosis-I :-
questions.explanation:
Answer: 1. 10 Pg
Correct Explanation:

\tG1 stage: The cell has 10 Pg of DNA.
\tS-phase: DNA is replicated, increasing the DNA content to 20 Pg.
\tMeiosis-I: Homologous chromosomes separate, but the DNA content in each daughter cell remains the same at 10 Pg, as the sister chromatids are still attached.

Thus, each daughter cell after meiosis-I will have 10 Pg of DNA.
Answer: 1. 10 Pg
